name: Black-winged Lovebird
rangeDescription: Highland forest of ethiopia
description: A small, short-tailed parrot that is mostly dark green. Males have a red patch above the bill and black underwings that are distinctive in flight.

name: Spotted Bamboowren
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (minas gerais) to northeastern argentina and (?) southeastern paraguay
description: Strange-looking small bird with a slender bill and a rather long tail. Found in bamboo stands in humid forests and second growth where it can be very hard to see.

name: Northern Brownbul
rangeDescription: Southwestern sudan; southeastern south sudan, southern ethiopia, and southern somalia to northern uganda, kenya, and northeastern tanzania
description: A drab, long-tailed brownish bird related to greenbuls. The tail is rufous and the throat paler buff.

name: Sagebrush Sparrow
rangeDescription: Sagebrush and saltbush of great basin
description: Pale, subtly-patterned sparrow. Sandy-brown overall with gray head and whitish breast with dark central spotting.

name: Finsch's Francolin
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed in congo, southwestern democratic republic of the congo and central angola
description: Medium-sized francolin with a mostly gray body, rufous head, and white throat. Found locally on the ground in grassy habitats including savanna, montane grassland, and woodland.

name: Unadorned Flycatcher
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of southern peru (cusco) to western bolivia
description: Dull, medium-sized flycatcher of montane forest. Greenish gray, with dull reddish wings that have weak reddish wing bars.

name: See-see Partridge
rangeDescription: Dry foothills and plateaus of southeastern turkey, northern syria, and (locally) northern saudi arabia to southern armenia, uzbekistan, southeastern turkmenistan, southern tajikistan southward through iran and afghanistan (except northeastern), to sub-himalayan pakistan
description: Eye-catching small gamebird of barren hills and wadis in arid and semi-arid areas. Note male’s black eyebrow, white ear patch, bright orange bill, and contrasting striped flanks.

name: Black-headed Myzomela
rangeDescription: Florida, savo, and guadalcanal (central solomon islands)
description: A distinctive myzomela with a relatively long downcurved bill and an entirely black face and throat forming a “mask.” Body yellowish and wings darker olive-green. Common in all habitats.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Spot-winged Starling
rangeDescription: Foothills of northern india and nepal; winters to myanmar and thailand
description: Uncommon pale-eyed starling with a white patch on each wing. Male is metallic dark blue-gray above with an orange breast and belly.

name: Sad Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Open woodland and montane forest of jamaica
description: A woodland species that often perches quietly three to ten meters above the ground; tends to lean forward on its perch. Note its relatively small bill and the lack of rust on the wings and tail.

name: Yellow-throated Leafbird
rangeDescription: Southwestern philippines (balabac, busuanga, palawan, and calamian)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland forest canopy and edge on Palawan and neighboring islands. Joins mixed-species flocks, often with bulbuls, foraging for fruits and seeds.

name: Rudd's Lark
rangeDescription: High-altitude grassland of eastern south africa
description: A small, stocky lark with an upright posture, a large head, and a short narrow tail. The back is spangled with tawny, black, and, white, and the head is boldly marked with a conspicuous eyebrow, an eye-ring, and a diagnostic pale central crown stripe.

name: Tristram's Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds and ranges hawaii, izu, and volcano islands
description: Dark brown, fork-tailed seabird of the northwestern and central Pacific, where it breeds on Japanese and Hawaiian islands. Generally forages far offshore and does not associate with boats.

name: Rufous-bellied Bush-Tyrant
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of southern peru (pasco) to western bolivia
description: Subtly patterned reddish-brown flycatcher of high-elevation montane forests. Perches upright, often on the tops of snags or bushes around forest edges and clearings.

name: Northern Bentbill
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern mexico (veracruz) to western panama
description: Tiny flycatcher of humid forest and woodland in tropical lowlands. Inconspicuous, mainly foraging at low to mid-levels in forest interior and edge, where flits from perch to perch and then sits still.

name: Zoe's Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Lowland forest of new guinea and larger satellite islands
description: A large pigeon of lowland and foothill forest. Pale gray head, yellow eye and short green tail.

name: Black-fronted Tern
rangeDescription: South island; disperses to stewart and north islands (new zealand)
description: A medium to small blue-gray tern endemic to New Zealand. Breeding birds have a black cap extending down to the bill and bright orange bill and legs.

name: Legge's Hawk-Eagle
rangeDescription: Southwestern india (western ghats) and sri lanka
description: Rather large, slim hawk-eagle with a white-tipped crest, streaked gray cheeks, and long feathered legs. It has strongly barred broad wings and a long tail.

name: Milky Stork
rangeDescription: Lowlands of malaya, indochina, greater sundas, and sulawesi
description: Large white stork with a yellow bill and reddish face and legs. Extensive black on the wings and tail only prominent in flight; a little of this black edging on the wings occasionally visible when the bird is foraging.

name: River Tern
rangeDescription: Pakistan to southern india, sri lanka, nepal, and southwestern china
description: Widespread inland tern of South and mainland Southeast Asia. Breeding adults have full black cap and pale gray wings; white belly, larger size, and heavier structure distinguishes this species from the less common Black-bellied Tern where their breeding ranges overlap.
